question: What happened to Paul and those who journeyed with him when the light shone?
choices: They all fell to the earth
explanation: Paul said, When we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice.

question: From whom did Paul receive authority and commission to go to Damascus?
explanation: Paul went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests.

question: From the power of whom did the Lord say people would be turned to God?
explanation: The Lord sent Paul to turn them from the power of Satan unto God.

question: What did the Lord say people would receive among them which are sanctified by faith?
explanation: The Lord said, That they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

question: What did Paul say people should do besides repent and turn to God?
explanation: Paul preached that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

question: What did Paul say Christ should shew unto the people and the Gentiles?
explanation: Paul said Christ should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

question: What did Festus say made Paul mad?
explanation: Festus said, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

question: Who rose up with Agrippa when Paul had finished?
explanation: When he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them.

question: What did Paul say he did to many of the saints in Jerusalem?
choices: Sent them out of the city
explanation: Paul said, Many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests.

question: Where did Paul say his manner of life was first spent among his own nation?
explanation: Paul said his manner of life from his youth was at the first among his own nation at Jerusalem.

question: What did Agrippa's company do when they had heard Paul?
choices: Went aside and talked among themselves
explanation: When they were gone aside, they talked between themselves.

question: Besides what he had seen, of what else was Paul to be a witness?
choices: Things in which the Lord would appear to him
explanation: The Lord said he would make Paul a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee.

question: What did Paul beseech King Agrippa to do?
explanation: Paul said, I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

question: What did Paul say he was exceedingly toward the saints before his conversion?
explanation: Paul said, being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

question: Who was the Macedonian of Thessalonica sailing with Paul?
explanation: One Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, was with them.

question: What did Julius allow Paul to do at Sidon?
choices: Go to his friends to refresh himself
explanation: Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

question: Whom did the centurion believe more than Paul about sailing on?
choices: The master and the owner of the ship
explanation: The centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

question: What did Paul say would be lost, but no man's life?
explanation: Paul said, There shall be no loss of any man's life among you, but of the ship.

question: Who stood by Paul in the night and said, Fear not?
choices: The Lord himself in a cloud
explanation: Paul said there stood by him the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, saying, Fear not, Paul.

question: What did Paul do in the presence of them all before he ate?
choices: Took bread and gave thanks to God
explanation: Paul took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all, and when he had broken it, he began to eat.

question: What was the soldiers' counsel about the prisoners?
choices: To kill them, lest any swim out and escape
To leave them on the ship
explanation: The soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

question: Who kept the soldiers from killing the prisoners?
explanation: The centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose.

question: What happened to everyone on board in the end?
choices: All were taken by another ship
They escaped all safe to land
explanation: They escaped all safe to land.

question: What was taken away when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days?
choices: All hope that they should be saved
explanation: When neither sun nor stars appeared in many days, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

question: Of what place was the ship that Paul and the prisoners first boarded?
explanation: They entered into a ship of Adramyttium, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia.

question: Why did they sail under Cyprus?
explanation: They sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

question: At Myra, what kind of ship did the centurion find to put them on?
choices: A ship of Tarsus bound for Rome
A ship of Sidon bound for Greece
A ship of Crete bound for Asia
A ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy
explanation: The centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

question: Why did Paul admonish them that sailing was now dangerous?
choices: Much time was spent and the fast was already past
explanation: When much time was spent, and sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them.

question: Why did most advise departing from Fair Havens?
choices: The haven was not commodious to winter in
explanation: Because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also.

question: What did they do with the boat at Clauda before undergirding the ship?
choices: Took it up with much work
explanation: Running under Clauda, they had much work to come by the boat: which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship.

question: What did they fear would happen when they struck sail?
explanation: Fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

question: What did Paul say after long abstinence about leaving Crete?
choices: They should have waited for the centurion
They should have sailed to Italy sooner
They should have hearkened and not left Crete
They should have sold the ship
explanation: Paul said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

question: What did the angel say God had given Paul?
choices: All them that sail with him
explanation: The angel said, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

question: What did Paul say about the island on which they must be cast?
choices: They must be cast upon a certain island
They would find a harbour at Crete
They would reach Rome by morning
explanation: Paul said, Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

question: What did the shipmen think at midnight on the fourteenth night?
choices: That the sun would soon rise
That they drew near to some country
explanation: About midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country.

question: What did the shipmen do under colour of casting anchors from the foreship?
choices: Let down the boat to flee the ship
Cut the ropes of the anchor
explanation: The shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors.

question: What did Paul say to the centurion and soldiers about the shipmen?
choices: Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved
They will carry us to land
explanation: Paul said, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

question: What did the soldiers do after Paul's warning?
choices: Cut off the ropes of the boat and let her fall off
explanation: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

question: What did Paul say would not fall from the head of any of them?
explanation: Paul said, There shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

question: In what city of Lycia did they come to land and change ships?
explanation: They came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

question: Near what city was The fair havens?
explanation: They came unto a place called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

question: Over against what place did they scarce come as the wind did not suffer them?
explanation: They sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us.

question: Under what island did they run when they had much work to come by the boat?
explanation: Running under a certain island which is called Clauda, they had much work to come by the boat.

question: What kind of wind blew softly just before the tempestuous wind arose?
explanation: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they sailed close by Crete.

question: What was the first depth they found with the sounding line?
explanation: They sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: a little further they found it fifteen fathoms.

question: How many anchors did they cast out of the stern?
explanation: They cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

question: How many days had they continued fasting when Paul urged them to eat?
explanation: Paul said, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

question: What did they cast into the sea after they had eaten enough?
explanation: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

question: What did they discover when the day came that they did not know the land?
explanation: They knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore.

question: Who was told to cast themselves into the sea first to get to land?
explanation: The centurion commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea.

question: How did the rest reach land who could not swim?
choices: By a rope from the shore
On the backs of the soldiers
Some on boards and some on broken pieces of the ship
explanation: The rest came some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship.

question: To which haven of Crete did most hope to reach to winter?
explanation: The more part advised to depart if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete.

question: In what sea were they driven up and down on the fourteenth night?
explanation: When the fourteenth night was come, we were driven up and down in Adria.

question: What did they loose when they hoised up the mainsail to the wind?
explanation: They took up the anchors, loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind.

question: How did the people of the island treat Paul and the others when they landed?
choices: They showed no little kindness and kindled a fire
They drove them back to the sea
explanation: The barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one.

question: What did the people say Paul must be when they saw the viper hang on his hand?
explanation: They said, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

question: What did Paul do with the viper?
choices: Shook it off into the fire
Held it up to the people
explanation: Paul shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

question: What did the people say about Paul when he came to no harm?
explanation: After they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

question: Who was the chief man of the island?
explanation: The chief man of the island, whose name was Publius, received them and lodged them three days courteously.

question: What happened to the others on the island who had diseases?
explanation: When this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed.

question: What did the brethren from Rome do when they heard of Paul's coming?
choices: Came to meet him as far as Appii Forum
explanation: The brethren came to meet us as far as Appii Forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

question: How was Paul allowed to dwell when they came to Rome?
choices: By himself with a soldier that kept him
explanation: Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

question: To whom did Paul say the salvation of God is sent?
explanation: Paul said, The salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

question: In what kind of ship did they depart from the island after three months?
explanation: After three months they departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle.

question: Why did the people of the island kindle a fire?
choices: Because of the present rain and the cold
explanation: They kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

question: What did the people expect to happen to Paul after the viper bit him?
choices: That he would swell or fall down dead
explanation: They looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly.

question: How long did Publius lodge Paul and his company?
explanation: Publius received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

question: What was wrong with the father of Publius?
choices: A fever and a bloody flux
explanation: The father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux.

question: How did Paul heal the father of Publius?
choices: He entered in, prayed, and laid his hands on him
explanation: Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

question: What did the islanders give them when they departed?
explanation: They honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

question: How long did the brethren at Puteoli ask Paul to stay with them?
explanation: At Puteoli they found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days.

question: What did Paul say the Romans would have done when they had examined him?
choices: Let him go, because there was no cause of death
explanation: When they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

question: Why did Paul say he was constrained to appeal unto Caesar?
choices: The Jews spake against his release
explanation: When the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar.

question: For what did Paul say he was bound with this chain?
explanation: Paul said, For the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

question: What did the Jews say they had received out of Judaea concerning Paul?
explanation: They said, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee.

question: What did the Jews say they knew about this sect?
choices: That it is spoken against everywhere
explanation: They said, As concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

question: How long did Paul expound and testify to those who came to his lodging?
explanation: Paul expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, from morning till evening.

question: How did the Jews respond to what Paul said?
choices: Some believed and some believed not
explanation: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

question: How did Paul preach in his own hired house?
choices: With all confidence, no man forbidding him
explanation: Paul preached the kingdom of God, and taught those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

question: What was the sign of the ship of Alexandria that wintered in the isle?
explanation: They departed in a ship of Alexandria, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

question: At which city did they tarry three days after leaving Melita?
explanation: Landing at Syracuse, they tarried there three days.

question: To which city did they come the day after the south wind blew?
explanation: After one day the south wind blew, and they came the next day to Puteoli.

question: Besides Appii Forum, where did the brethren meet Paul?
explanation: The brethren came to meet them as far as Appii Forum, and The three taverns.

question: To whom did the centurion deliver the prisoners at Rome?
explanation: When we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard.

question: After how many days did Paul call the chief of the Jews together?
explanation: After three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together.

question: What did the Jews say none of the brethren out of Judaea had done concerning Paul?
choices: Shewed or spake any harm of him
explanation: They said, Neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

question: What did the Jews say they desired to hear from Paul?
explanation: They said, We desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest.

question: What did Paul say at the end that the Holy Ghost spoke by Esaias?
choices: Arise, shine, for thy light is come
Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear
explanation: Paul said, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers.

question: What did Paul say had grown dull about the people?
explanation: Paul quoted that their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed.

question: How did the Jews depart after Paul spoke?
explanation: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

question: Why did they depart from Paul after he had spoken one word?
choices: They were afraid of the soldier
explanation: When they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word.

question: Who did Paul receive in his own hired house?
choices: All that came in unto him
explanation: Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him.

question: Where did many come to Paul on the day appointed?
explanation: There came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God.

question: What did Paul say the Jews would not do lest they be converted?
choices: See, hear, or understand with the heart
explanation: Paul quoted, Lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
